claims.claim: Letter of John of Raithu: 'Ad sanctum Joannem virum admirandum, asceterio in monte Sina praefectum ... Joannes peccator Raithuni monasterii antistes'; asks 'uti nobis rudibus per litteras aperias quae ad veteris exemplum Mosis in eodem monte divino spectaculo dignatus inspexisti', tablets that lead those 'qui ad coelum enituntur, veluti per scalarum gradus'; 'Nam si Jacob ovium duntaxat custos, tremendum ejusmodi in scala spectaculum contemplatus est, quanto magis gregis ratione pollentis magister ... ad Deum iter omnibus [ostendet]'
claims.witness: PG88 l.43690-43697 (OCR 'Ad sancitum', 'pecca- tori ... anstites'), 43736-43741, 43810-43823 (OCR 'ascendet' for the last verb)

claims.claim: Reply: 'me nisi metus et ingens periculum, ne sanctae obedientiae, virtutum omnium parentis jugum et imperium abjicerem, coercuisset, tam temerarium nunquam futurum fuisse, ut onus, quod impar humeris vires meas excedit, vel susciperem, vel tentarem'
claims.witness: PG88 l.43833 (heading 'Respondet Climacus Joanni Raithuni cenobii antistiti'), 43869-43876

claims.claim: Labbe's notice: 'Joannes Climacus, ob librum 30 capitum, quibus tanquam gradibus ... ascenditur, sic vulgo nuncupatus, idem quoque Joannes Sinaita, vel abbas sancti Montis Sina, cognomento Scholasticus'; 'Vixit extremo Christi seculo sexto circa annum 580, et si Menaeis Graecorum fides, pene centenarius obiit die 30 Martii'
claims.witness: PG88 l.41317-41331 (heading 'Phil. Labbe, Dissertatio historica de S. Joanne Climaco')

claims.claim: Title of Rader's edition: 'Joannis Scholastici, vulgo Climaci, abbatis montis Sina, opera omnia, interprete Matthaeo Radero'; Rader, Isagoge cap. 1: 'Hic cognoscis eumdem esse S. Joannem abbatem montis Sina, cognomento Scholasticum, et Joannem Sinaitam, et Joannem Climacum'

Daniel's Life, title 'Vita compendio conscripta abbatis Joannis antistitis sancti montis Sina, cognomento Scholastici ... a Daniele monacho ... e coenobio Rhaitheno'; 'Quae patria nobilisve civitas heroem hunc progenuerit, et ante susceptam ... religiosae vitae palaestram, educarit, pro certo et explorato non habeo dicere'

Daniel: 'cum flos aevi ... sextum jam decimum aetatis annum agitaret ... seipsum ... Deo ... sacrificium obtulit; quando corpus quidem in hunc Sinaeum ... intulit'; 'cervicemque peritissimo animorum rectori ... submisit'; 'omnibus litterarum disciplinis esset initiatus'; Rader's note (g): 'Hinc sortitus est nomen Scholastici'

Daniel: 'Jam vicesimum annum exorsus, cum praemisso ad caelestem imperatorem suo praeside tanquam legato et patrono ... in stadium vitae quietae et solitariae ... ingreditur; locoque, cui Tholas nomen, certamini ad quintum ab aede sacra lapidem delecto, quadraginta ipsos annos inibi ... traduxit'

Daniel, the rock: Moses at noon in August ('sextilis enim ultimus in aestate mensium erat') sleeps under 'immane saxum'; John 'tantum pauxillum conniveret, aspicit virum humana specie augustiorem ... « Hem [OCR 'liane'], Joannes, tu securus hic stertis, et Moses vita periclitatur? »'; Moses that evening: 'Immane saxum ... dormitantem minimo minus oppressisset'

Daniel: 'fuere qui invidiae oestro perciti garrulum nugatoremque appellitarent ... per totius anni spatium tam altum siluit, ut ipsi illius calumniatores supplices ad illum ... adirent, ne vellet perennem utilitatis fontem obturare'; 'omnes ... tanquam alterum quemdam Moysen ad coenobii praefecturam vi pertraxerunt'

Ladder, step 1 'De abdicatione vitae saecularis'; step 30 ends 'Nunc autem manent haec tria, fides, spes, charitas; major autem horum est charitas'; 'Ascendite fratres, ascendite alacriter'; Christ 'qui cum esset, ut videbatur, triginta annorum baptizatus, tricesimum gradum in scala spirituali sortitus est: quandoquidem Deus est charitas'
Book to the Shepherd: heading 'Coenobiarcha pastori, navarcho, medico, litteratori comparatur'; 'Pastor ille verus ... Gubernator ... Medicus ... Doctor est'

Bollandists: Daniel wrote the Life 'mox ab ejusdem obitu ... cum hujus Abbas Joannes adhuc viveret'; the Menologium of Basil: 'cum sextum decimum annum ageret, ascendit in montem Sina ... post decimum nonum inde annum se solitudini tradidit in loco, cui Tholas nomen fuit, quinto lapide a basilica'; commemorated 'xxx Martii'

Rader's epitome: 'Post decimum nonum inde annum ad stadium solitudinis (Tholas loco nomen fuit) quinto lapide a basilica remoto se contulit'; note '(a) Haec Vitae epitome est e Danielis vita extracta'

Sinai monk's appendix (Rader: '(a) A monacho aliquo Sinaita synchrono haec'; Bollandists: 'Auctore monacho Sinaita, Synchrono'): Martyrius tonsured him; Anastasius foretold 'antistitem montis Sina'; 'post quadraginta annos Joannes creatus est praeses noster et abbas'; John the Sabaite washed his feet; Strategius at his tonsure 'cum annum aetatis vicesimum ageret'

Sinai monk on George: 'Sciendum Climaco fuisse germanum fratrem Georgium, quem sibi Climacus vivo successorem destinavit'; John: 'non patiar ut annum hunc absolvas, quin me sequaris. Quod et factum est; intra decimum enim mensem et ipse Georgius ad Dominum profectus est'
claims.witness: PG88 l.43008-43037 (Greek 'δέκα μηνῶν', OCR 'čéxa pnvov', l.43027); AS Mar. 3 l.210128-210145 reads 'Intra decimum enim annum'

claims.claim: Labbe on Antonius Magister's reckoning: born 'anno circiter 525', monk at sixteen, died 'Christi 605 aut 606'; 'subductis rationibus peccasse Magistrum'

Labbe: from the Sinai monk (as Magister reports him, 'sub finem capitis XV'), John died, George learned four months later that Peter, patriarch of Jerusalem, would die in six months, and both died 'decimo post transitum Joannis Climaci mense'; Theophanes gives Peter's end at 566; Evagrius and Nicephorus are set against it; so 'si vera narravit anonymus Sinaita monachus, Joannis Climaci mortem ... inter annos Christianae aerae 560 et 565 quaerendam esse, non vero in annum 586 rejiciendam'; 'vix certi quidquam de anno mortis Climaci, multoque minus de profectione ejus in coenobium, de tempore commorationis in eremo, de praefecturae Sinaiticae primordiis pronuntiari posse'; the tale as Rader and the Bollandists print it names no Peter (PG88 l.42850-43037; AS Mar. 3 l.210071-210145)
claims.witness: PG88 l.41392-41420, 41474-41495 (OCR '569' at l.41415, against the sequence the note gives; OCR 'zr» 560 ce 565', '5856')

claims.claim: Bollandists: 'Philippus Labbe de Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis S. Joannem Climacum scribit obiisse circa annum 580, quod verosimile nobis est, aut saltem sub finem istius seculi'

Gregory to John, abbot of Mount Sinai: 'Sanctitatem vitae tuae humilitatis tuae testatur epistola'; beds and bedding for the 'hierocomium, quod a quodam illic Isauro constructum est'; Ewald-Hartmann head it '600, (Sept. 1.)' and note 'De Iohannis Climaci vita et operibus cf. M. Raderi editionem apud Migne, patrol. Gr. t. 88'
claims.witness: Ewald-Hartmann l.7718-7745, 7773 (OCR 'ahhati monti^ Sinai', 'Baderi'); the file header warns its OCR is second witness only

claims.claim: Barmby: 'Gregory to John, Abbot of Mount Sina'; note: 'No doubt the John called Climacus, Scholasticus, and Sinaita ... he is said to have retired thence to live the life of an anchoret, to have been elected abbot at the age of 75, to have again after a time retired into solitude, and to have died early in the 7th century'; 'constructed by one Isaurus there'

Moschus, Spiritual Meadow 127 (index 'CXXVII. Vita abbatis Georgii sancti montis Sina'; the chapter head in the text reads 'CAPUT CXXVI'): George writes to the patriarch Peter 'post sex menses Christo Domino ac Deo nostro simul occursuri sumus'; both died after six months
Rader on the George of Moschus: 'Georgius quidam, haud scio an idem Climaci frater ... (diversum tamen crediderim), quem Joannes Eviratus seu Moschus in suo Viridario spirituali laudat'

Trithemius dated him under Constantine's sons; Labbe: 'Errat Joannes Trithemius ... Certum quippe est vixisse post S. Sabbam ... qui e vita migravit quinto Decembris anni 532'; Rader and the Bollandists likewise

Labbe: the Greeks held him in great value, 'ut ex Athanasii quaestionibus, Elia Cretensi, Theodoro Studita, Philippo Solitario, Joanne Zonara, aliisque constat'; Elias of Crete 'qui explanationes in Scalam scripsit'

Labbe: Ladder 'Latine primum reddita fuisse dicitur an. 1295, ab Angelo de Cingulo O. M. qui Clarenus cognominatus est'; Venice 1590 'in Graeco-barbaram seu vulgarem linguam translatus a Maximo [OCR 'Marzunio'] episcopo Citherorum'
Baronius, quoted by Rader: 'Porro animi illius divina quaedam effigies multo clarius perspicitur in scriptis ejus'
Rader against Gerson: 'nihil falsum est in toto Climaco, nihil contra Ecclesiae decreta aut male explicatum, sed potius male intellectum'
Labbe: another John, abbot of Sinai, named in manuscripts as author of Barlaam and Josaphat; Rader holds Climacus is not its author
claims.witness: PG88 l.41465-41470, 41747-41754 (OCR 'pen' for 'non'); PG94 l.8845-8846 ('Joannes Climacus historiae Barlaam et Josaphat auctor non est')

claims.claim: Thomas à Kempis, Life of John Cacabus (Ketel), cook in the House of Florentius: 'Sometimes he read the book of John Climacus "On perfect renunciation of the world and mortification of the Will," and expounded therefrom sentiments full of spiritual truth, so that wise men marvelled that he had so good an understanding of the book'
Rader: 'Proinde vere Bellarminus anno 530 collocavit'

Oliger prints Bartholomew of Pisa: 'loannem Climacum de graeco transtulit in latinum' (of Angelo of Cingoli); Bernardino of Aquila, Chronica Fratrum Min. Observantiae: 'Iste liber in nostra familia magnae reputationis habetur'; Mariano of Florence: 'librum Sancti lohannis Climaci traduxit'

Barmby: the name from 'Scala (κλὶμαξ) Paradisi, whence his name of Climacus'; gifts '15 cloaks, 30 rachanæ ... and 15 beds'; note: rachana 'usually supposed to mean some woollen article of dress, worn by monks. Others understand blankets'
Raithu placed: 'De Raithu vicino monasterio versus Rubrum-mare'
Labbe: 'Vixit extremo Christi seculo sexto circa annum 580'; Bollandists: 'seculo Christi sexto floruit'

contested_claims.claim: When he died
sides: Library header of the PG88 file: c.579-649 (PG88 l.7); a header, not a source
Labbe: lived about 580 (PG88 l.41330); if the Sinai monk's tale, as Antonius Magister retells it (l.41392-41394), is true, died 560-565; hardly anything certain (l.41486-41495)
Antonius Magister, as Labbe reports: died 605 or 606 (l.41376-41381)
Bollandists: Labbe's 580 likely, or at least the end of the sixth century (AS Mar. 3 l.209545-209551)
Barmby: he is said to have died early in the seventh century (NPNF2/13 l.5357-5363)
Bellarmine, as Rader reports: about 530 (PG88 l.41752)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Gregory's John, abbot of Mount Sinai, in 600, is Climacus
sides: Barmby: 'No doubt' (NPNF2/13 l.5357)
Ewald-Hartmann: point to Rader's edition for his life (l.7773)
Labbe's 560-565 would put his death at least 35 years before the letter (arithmetic on PG88 l.41489-41490 and Ewald-Hartmann l.7719)

contested_claims.claim: How long he lived in the monastery before going to Tholas
sides: Rader's Latin of Daniel: 'Jam vicesimum annum exorsus' (PG88 l.42287-42288)
Rader's epitome and the Menologium of Basil: nineteen years after coming to Sinai (PG88 l.43087; AS Mar. 3 l.209402)
Sinai monk: tonsured at twenty (PG88 l.42888-42890); Rader's note (c): sixteen is his entry as a novice (l.42188-42194)

contested_claims.claim: How long George outlived him
sides: Rader's Latin and Greek: within ten months (PG88 l.43027, 43036-43037)
Bollandists' Latin: within ten years (AS Mar. 3 l.210144)
Both texts share John's promise: 'non patiar ut annum hunc absolvas, quin me sequaris' (PG88 l.43034-43035; AS l.210142-210143); the brief tells only this

contested_claims.claim: Whether Moschus's George of Sinai is his brother
sides: Labbe: Moschus tells nearly the same of George and Peter's death (PG88 l.41486-41489)
Rader: rather a different man (l.43040-43044)

Cave calls Julian 'presbyterum Romanum' and says the collection runs 'a Siricio ad Anastasium II' (OCR 'Anastesium IH'). The brief calls Julian 'a Roman priest' and leaves out the Gelasius line for length.

claims.claim: Letter to Eugippius: 'beati Gregorii Nysseni episcopi librum De Conditione hominis e Graeca locutione converti'; 'Et quia sunt, ut dixi, aliqua quae possunt merito reprehendi, nullus lector in his meum putet obligatum esse consensum; quia officio translatoris explicui, non censoris judicio comprobavi' (OCR 'oflicio trauslaloris', 'comproba vi.' on the next line)

First Easter letter, to Petronius: 'Paschalis festi rationem, quam multorum diu frequenter a nobis exposcit instantia, nunc adjuti precibus vestris explicare curavimus: sequentes per omnia venerabilium trecentorum et octodecim pontificum, qui apud Nicaeam ...'; 'Quia vero sanctus Cyrillus primum cyclum ab anno Diocletiani centesimo quinquagesimo tertio coepit ... nos a ducentesimo quadragesimo octavo anno ejusdem tyranni potius quam principis inchoantes, noluimus circulis nostris memoriam impii et persecutoris innectere; sed magis elegimus ab Incarnatione Domini nostri Jesu Christi annorum tempora praenotare: quatenus exordium spei nostrae notius nobis existeret, et causa reparationis humanae, id est passio Redemptoris nostri, evidentius eluceret.' The brief tells this in reported speech, keeping both purpose clauses. Round 1: the brief drops 'the cause of our renewal' for length and adds 'he wrote'; both purpose clauses stay.
claims.witness: Dionysius, Epistola I de ratione Paschae (pl67 l.1102-1165)

Mommsen's Marius lists 'a. 525 Probo iuniore et Philoxeno. Ind. III.' (chron-min-2 l.21310).

Cave: 'In hoc cyclo annos a Christi Incarnatione numeravit Dionysius: atque istam aeram primus omnium annis supputandis adhibuit' (OCR ':eram', 'adhibu.t')

Plummer: 'In chronology Bede has the enormous merit of being the first chronicler who gave the date from Christ's birth, in addition to the year of the world; and thus introduced the use of the Dionysian Era into Western Europe ... It was not used in papal documents till the eleventh century' (two-column OCR, text re-joined)
Brehaut: 'Isidore shows no signs of being aware of the proposal of Dionysius Exiguus for an era beginning with the birth of Christ'; 'he was acquainted with the essentials of his Easter table'

Hodgkin: 'the so-called Dionysius Exiguus, who fixed (erroneously, as it now appears) the era of the birth of Christ, and whose system of chronology founded on this event has been accepted by all the nations of Christendom'

claims.claim: Bede, De temporum ratione, as quoted: 'sed Dionysius venerabilis abbas Romanae urbis, et utriusque linguae, Graecae videlicet et Latinae, non ignobili praeditus scientia, paschales scribens circulos, noluit eis, sicut ipse testatur, memoriam impii persecutoris innectere'; chronicle: 'Dionysius paschales scribit circulos incipiens ab anno dominicae Incarnationis 532'. Bede's own works are not held apart from the History; these lines are known through the PL 67 testimonia.
Bellarmine, as quoted: 'vixit tempore Theodorici regis Italiae, et successorum ejus'

Janus on Cassiodorus as sole witness: 'Inter aequales solus fere Cassiodorus virtutum illius memoriam conservavit, quem unum omnes qui hucdum aliquid de vita Dionysii tradiderunt, auctorem secuti sunt' (OCR 'colus fere'); on abbot: 'Abbatem plerique vocant, quem Cassiodorus monachum dixit. Sed monasterium cujus abbas fuerit ignorari'; Pagi 'abbatis dignitatem Dionysio plane derogat, eique a Beda primum afflictam fuisse contendit'; Felix abbot of Gillitanum's prologue of 616 calls him abbot of Rome; 'honoris potius quam muneris causa, abbas dictus est'
Mommsen: 'Victorii Aquitani ea aetate ante editum alterum Dionysii Exigui in Italia communi consensu receptum'
Percival: 'Somewhere about the year 500 Dionysius Exiguus, who was Abbot of a Monastery in Rome, translated a collection of Greek Canons into Latin for Bishop Stephen of Salona'
Duchesne: 'La collection de Denys le Petit, telle qu'elle fut envoyée à Charlemagne par le pape Hadrien'
De cursu et saltu lunae, printed with Alcuin: 'Inde Dionysius dicit: A primo anno, qui non habet epactas lunares...', footnote 'Dionysius Exiguus, epist. ad Bonifacium et Bonum'

Cave on Proclus: 'Oratio Procli de laudibus Deiparae (quam tamen non ab Exiguo, sed a Mario Mercatore, versam esse contendit Garnerius ...)'; 'Proclus Constantinopolitanus episcopus' identifies Proclus
He signs himself 'Dionysius Exiguus' in the addresses of his prefaces and letters; not used in the brief

contested_claims.claim: Whether the count of years from the Incarnation spread from Dionysius
sides: Cave: Dionysius 'primus omnium' used this era (pl67 l.500-502); Janus: his cycle brought in the era still used, and holds the common view (pl67 l.36705-36708, 36823-36825); Hodgkin: his chronology accepted by all Christendom (hodgkin l.3431-3434)

Janus's note: others make the era later than Dionysius and credit Bede's authority (pl67 l.36727-36730); Plummer: Bede introduced the Dionysian era into Western Europe, and papal documents did not use it till the eleventh century (plummer l.2666-2688); Brehaut: Isidore shows no sign of knowing it (brehaut l.6743-6745); Janus also reports Hardouin's view that the era was older than Dionysius, in use early in the fifth century, and argues against it (pl67 l.36730-36760)

claims.claim: History of the Franks V.37: 'Hoc tempore et beatus Martinus Galliciensis episcopus obiit, magnum populo illi faciens planctum. Nam hic Pannoniae ortus fuit; et exinde ad visitanda loca sancta in Oriente properans, in tantum se litteris imbuit, ut nulli secundus suis temporibus haberetur. Exinde Gallitiam venit, ubi cum beati Martini reliquiae portarentur, episcopus ordinatur. In quo sacerdotio impletis plus minus triginta annis, plenus virtutibus migravit ad Dominum. Versiculos, qui super ostium sunt a parte meridiana in basilica sancti Martini, ipse composuit'
claims.witness: arndt-krusch1885 l.18175-18181 (OCR 'planctura', 'Nara'); Dalton's English, dalton1927 l.9925-9932 and 9940-9941; Caspari numbers the chapter V.38 (caspari1883 l.267-269)

claims.claim: Gregory wrote the Virtues of Martin I.11 while Martin lived: 'qui ibidem nunc sacerdos habetur'; the Bollandists: 'Haec S. Gregorius scripsit ante annum DLXXX, quando scilicet in Gallicia S. Martinus vivebat Episcopus'

Epitaph: 'Pannoniis genitus, transcendens aequora vasta, Galliciae in gremium divinis nutibus actus, Confessor, Martine, tua hac dicatus in aula Antistes, cultum instituit ritumque sacrorum; Teque, patrone, sequens famulus Martinus eodem Nomine, non merito, hic in Christi pace quiesco'
claims.witness: PL72 l.3432-3439 (OCR 'geuitus', 'eqiiora', 'quieseo'); acta-sanctorum martii-3 l.31525-31535; caspari1883 l.786-789 ('hic in pace Christi quiesco'); first line also in Perez's note, PL83 l.122465-122472

claims.claim: Fortunatus, Poems V.2: 'Martino servata novo, Gallicia, plaude: sortis apostolicae vir tuus iste fuit'; 'Pannoniae, ut perhibent, veniens e parte Quiritis est magis effectus Gallisueba salus'; V.1 heading 'Ad Martinum episcopum Galliciae', salutation '... in Christi regis exercitu post ducem Paulum primipilo Martino episcopo Fortunatus'

Isidore, On Famous Men 35: 'Martinus, Dumiensis monasterii sanctissimus pontifex, ex Orientis partibus navigans, in Galleciam venit, ibique conversis ab Ariana impietate ad fidem catholicam Suevorum populis regulam fidei et sanctae religionis constituit, ecclesias confirmavit, monasteria condidit, copiosaque praecepta piae institutionis composuit. Cujus quidem ego ipse legi librum de Differentiis quatuor virtutum, et aliud volumen Epistolarum ... Floruit, regnante Theodemiro rege Suevorum'
claims.witness: PL83 l.122413-122429, 122440-122442 (CAPUT XXXV, nn.45-46; Caspari and the Bollandists cite it as c.22, caspari1883 l.392-395, acta-sanctorum martii-3 l.31039-31052)

claims.claim: Isidore, History of the Sueves 90-91: 'Multis deinde Suevorum regibus in Ariana haeresi permanentibus, tandem regni potestatem Theudemirus suscepit. Qui confestim, Arianae impietatis errore destructo, Suevos catholicae fidei reddidit, innitente Martino, monasterii Dumiensis episcopo, fide et scientia claro, cujus studio et pax Ecclesiae ampliata est'
claims.witness: PL83 l.120277-120286 (two columns interleaved in OCR); mommsen1894 l.29502-29507

claims.claim: Isidore, Chronicle: 'Per idem tempus Martinus, Bracarensis episcopus, apud Galleciam prudentia et doctrina catholicae fidei clarus habetur'
claims.witness: PL83 l.117431-117433 (OCR 'Dracarensis'); variant reading cited mommsen1894 l.43733

claims.claim: John of Biclaro: 'In provincia Gallaeciae Miro post Theudemirum Suevorum rex efficitur'; under Mommsen's '585?': 'Leovegildus rex Gallaecias vastat, Audecanem regem comprehensum regno privat, Suevorum gentem, thesaurum et patriam in suam redigit potestatem et Gothorum provinciam facit'

First Council of Braga: 'CONCILIUM BRACARENSE PRIMUM OCTO EPISCOPORUM HABITUM ERA DXCIX. ANNO TERTIO ARIAMIRI REGIS'; bishops 'Lucretius, Andreas, Martinus, Cottus, Ildericus, Lucetius, Timotheus, Maliosus'; 'Martinus episcopus subscripsi' third, with no see

Second Council of Braga, 'anno secundo regis Mironis ... era DCX': 'Martinus Bracarensis ecclesiae episcopus dixit' first; 'quia opitulante Christi gratia de unitate et rectitudine fidei in hac provincia nihil est dubium, illud modo nobis specialius est agendum, ut si quid ... reprehensibile invenitur in nobis, recurrentes ad testimonia sanctarum scripturarum vel antiquorum canonum instituta ... corrigamus'; 'Martinus Bracarensis metropolitanae ecclesiae episcopus his gestis subscripsi' first
claims.witness: Hispana l.56907-56920, 56949-56955 (OCR damaged: 'rid fO EE Iii est dubium'), 57238-57239; clean in acta-sanctorum martii-3 l.31097-31136

claims.claim: Capitula Martini, preface to 'Nitigi episcopo vel universo concilio Lucensis ecclesiae': canons from the East 'graeco prius sermone conscripti ... postea ... in latinam linguam translati', translators and copyists left them obscure, so 'simpliciüs et emendatis restaurem' (OCR; read 'emendatius'), clergy and laity in separate parts

Tenth Council of Toledo: 'testamentum gloriosae memoriae sancti Martini ecclesiae Bracarensis episcopi, qui et Dumiense monasterium visus est construxisse ... ut succedentibus per ordinem regibus ad complementum ejus ipsius testamenti constitutio commendata maneret'
claims.witness: Hispana l.46500-46515 (running head 'C. TOLETANUM X.' l.46455); quoted in full by Caspari l.751-757 and the Bollandists l.31252-31266

claims.claim: Letter to Polemius: 'Epistolam tuae sanctae caritatis accepi, in qua scripsisti ad me, ut pro castigatione rusticorum, qui, adhuc pristina paganorum superstitione detenti, cultum uenerationis plus demoniis, quam deo persoluunt, aliqua de origine idolorum et sceleribus ipsorum uel pauca de multis ad te scripta dirigerem'; 'cibum rusticis rustico sermone condire. Ita ergo, opitulante tibi deo, erit tuae praedicationis exordium'; Polemius signs Braga II as 'Polimius Asturicensis ecclesiae episcopus'
claims.witness: caspari1883 l.3700-3712 (OCR 'tus sanct® caritatis', 'tus pradicationis'); Hispana l.57276; Caspari's note on Astorga l.3724-3726

claims.claim: Sermon ch.15-16: 'Uos ergo, fideles, qui ... ad Christi baptismum accessistis'; 'quomodo aliqui ex uobis, qui abrenuntiauerunt diabolo et angelis eius et culturis eius et operibus eius malis, modo iterum ad culturas diaboli reuertuntur? Nam ad petras et ad arbores et ad fontes et per triuia cereolos incendere, quid est aliud, nisi cultura diaboli?'

Formula vitae honestae addressed 'Mironi regi Martinus humilis episcopus'; its opening 'Quatuor virtutum species ... prudentia, ... magnanimitas, ... continentia, ... justitia'; the Bollandists identify it with Isidore's book on the four virtues
Caspari: born 'etwa im zweiten Decennium des sechsten Jahrhunderts'; came to Galicia 'Um 550', by combining Gregory's passages; died 580; feast 20 March
Caspari: Gregory's having him made bishop on arrival 'ist ein Irrthum Gregors'; Martin first founded Dumio and was its abbot
Caspari: the ten Capitula and 'aller Wahrscheinlichkeit nach auch die Acten' of Braga II come from Martin; he presented the ten capitula, which he and the bishops signed
Caspari dates De correctione rusticorum 'in die Zeit zwischen 572 und 574'
Paschasius's prologue as Caspari quotes it: 'Martinus episcopus transtulit per manum Paschasii diaconi interrogationes ... in Dumiensi coenobio'; 'sicut in dato mihi codice ea scripta, sic transtuli'
Caspari traces the sermon's use by Eligius, Pirminius, Aelfric's homily and an Old Norse (Icelandic) sermon

The Bollandists: Gregory's death notice falls in Childebert's fifth year, 'convenit in annum Christi DLXXX'; the thirty years 'errore quodam amanuensium intrusi sunt pro annis plus minus viginti'; the king converted 'Theodomirus sive Ariamirus, qui magis corrupte Chararicus appellatur a Gregorio'; his move to Braga 'at quo anno non liquet'; feast 'ad terium decimum Kalendas Aprilis', kept by Braga and Évora 'uti ex earum Breviariis liquet'

Note signed 'R.' in Arndt's HF V.37: 'Fuit episcopus, primo Dumiensis monasterii (Mondonedo), tum Bracarensis; qua dignitate non 30, sed 20 circiter annis potitus est. Festivitas eius recolitur die 20. Martii ... R.'; Dalton: 'About 580, on 20th March'; Krusch on VM I.11: 'Obiit a. 580'
claims.witness: arndt-krusch1885 l.18215-18217 (HF ed. Arndt, VM ed. Krusch: contents l.138, 140); dalton1927 l.9934; arndt-krusch1885 l.46065

claims.claim: Krusch on VM I.11: 'Chararicum regem Gallaeciensem nemo laudavit nisi Gregorius ... plerique Chararicum eundem ac Theudemirum fuisse coniecerunt, qui in actis conciliorum constanter Ariamirus appellatus est ... verisimilius est, illum potius filium Chararici, non Chararicum ipsum fuisse'
Perez's note in PL83: founded Dumio 'ut dicitur in decimo concil. Tolet.'; 'subscribit Martinus episcopus in concil. primo Bracar., anno Christi 561'; archbishop of Braga at Braga II

Where the verses stood: Dalton 'i.e. at Tours'; Caspari reports Hieronymus de Prato for Tours, Florez and Mabillon for the Galician church of Martin, 'nach dem Letzteren in Dumio, nach dem Ersteren in Orense'
Where the epitaph stood: Bollandists 'in ecclesia S. Martini Turonensis a Theodomiro Rege constructa'; Caspari 'in der von Chararich erbauten basilica sancti Martini'

Gallandi's notice quotes Mabillon: 'Martinum alii Pannonium a patria, alii Gallicensem a provincia ... Dumiensem et Bracarensem alii a sedibus quibus episcopus praefuit, cognominarunt'; Tamayo noted that Baronius 'de unico Martino tres conflasse'
Martin's verses in the basilica of Martin of Tours: 'Tua signa Suevus admirans didicit fidei quo tramite pergat ... teneat Gallaecia tota patronum'

Caspari: Martin came to Galicia 'Um 550'; Dumio lay 'in der nächsten Nähe von Bracara'; Polemius sat at Braga II 'im Jahre 572'; Bollandists: Braga II 'Era DCX, sive anno Christi DLXXII'; Dalton: 'the Suevi settled in Spain'
Childebert II: Caspari 'im fünften Jahre Childeberts des Zweiten oder im Jahre 580'; Bollandists 'ad annum quintum Childeberti Regis Austrasiorum Francorum'

contested_claims.claim: Which Suevic king turned to the Catholic faith
sides: Gregory of Tours: Chararic, on the healing of his son (arndt-krusch1885 l.45603-45605, 46026-46028)
Isidore of Seville: Theudemir, with Martin's backing (PL83 l.120280-120284)
Braga I acts: the reigning king is Ariamir, in his third year (Hispana l.56276-56279)
Krusch: Chararic named by Gregory alone; Theudemir more likely Chararic's son (arndt-krusch1885 l.45634-45640)
Caspari: two different kings, Chararic the earlier, 'ohne jedoch in der Sache ganz sicher zu sein' (caspari1883 l.455-463)
Bollandists: Theodomir or Ariamir, called Chararic by Gregory in a corrupt form (acta-sanctorum martii-3 l.30887-30889)

contested_claims.claim: How long he was bishop
sides: Gregory: 'plus minus triginta annis' (arndt-krusch1885 l.18180)
Bollandists: a copyist's thirty for about twenty (acta-sanctorum martii-3 l.30879-30883)
Note signed R. in Arndt's HF: 'non 30, sed 20 circiter' (arndt-krusch1885 l.18215-18216)

contested_claims.claim: When he became bishop
sides: Gregory: ordained bishop when the relics came (arndt-krusch1885 l.18178-18179; l.46027)
Caspari: an error of Gregory's; first abbot of Dumio (caspari1883 l.307-309)

contested_claims.claim: Where his verses over the south door stood
sides: Dalton: at Tours (dalton1927 l.26883-26885)
Hieronymus de Prato, as Caspari reports: Tours (caspari1883 l.195-196)
Mabillon, as Caspari reports: the Galician church of Martin at Dumio; Florez: at Orense (caspari1883 l.197-199)

contested_claims.claim: Where Dumio was
sides: Caspari: close to Braga, after Gallandi 'vix uno milliari' (caspari1883 l.448-450, 487)
Note signed R. in Arndt's HF: 'Dumiensis monasterii (Mondonedo)' (arndt-krusch1885 l.18215)

contested_claims.claim: Who built the church where the epitaph was to stand
sides: Caspari: Chararic (caspari1883 l.762)
Bollandists: Theodomir, whom they take to be Gregory's Chararic (acta-sanctorum martii-3 l.31521-31522, 30887-30889)

claims.claim: Adomnan III.17 (Huyshe): 'four holy founders of monas-teries, coming over from Ireland to visit St. Columba, found him in Hinba island ... Comgell Mocu Aridi, Cainnech Mocu Dalan, Brendan Mocu Alti, Cormac-Ua-Liathain. These with one accord agreed that St. Columba should consecrate the sacred mysteries of the Eucharist in the church in their presence'; 'while the solemnity of the Mass was being celebrated, St. Brendan Mocu Alti, as he afterwards told Comgell and Cainnech, saw a certain blazing and most luminous globe of fire burning over St. Columba's head and rising up like a pillar as he stood before the altar consecrating the Holy Oblation until the same most holy ministrations were completed'
claims.witness: adomnan huyshe1905 l.10226-10251 (Huyshe's bracket on Hinba, '[Eilean-na-Naoimh, one of the Garveloch Isles?]', is his)

claims.claim: Adomnan I.26 (Huyshe): 'Aidan by name, son of Fergno, a most religious man who, as is said, ministered for twelve years to Brendan Mocualti'

Huyshe's notes: 'St. Brendan, of Clonfert. Mac-Ua-Alti was his clan name'; 'He was St. Brendan the famous voyager, founder of Clonfert, commemorated in the Calendar May 16. Kerry was the principal district of his race, the Kiarraighe. Born 482, founded Clonfert 559, died 577. His day is May 16'; introduction: 'In 577 died St. Brendan of Clonfert'

Adomnan III.3 and III.11 (Huyshe): 'St. Brendan, the founder of that monastery which is called in Irish Birra' kisses the excommunicated Columba; Columba sees angels meet 'the soul of the holy Brendan', founder of Birr; Huyshe: 'He must be distinguished from Brendan, founder of Clonfert ... St. Brendan of Birr died in 573'; 'He died c. 573 in the eightieth year of his age'
Annales Cambriae: 'cxxx. Annus. Brendan Byror dormitatio'; editor's introduction: 'the death of Brenda, abbot of Birre'

claims.claim: Stokes: 'The Book of Lismore was compiled from the lost Book of Monaster-boice and other manuscripts, in the latter half of the fifteenth century'; its Lives are 'a mixed language, in which Old-Irish forms appear side by side with those belonging to the late Middle, and even Modern, periods'
claims.witness: stokes lismore1890 l.218-219, 3254-3257; contents 'Life of Brenainn, son of Finnlugh' l.134

claims.claim: Lismore Life (Stokes's English): 'the seventh of the calends of June, was Brenainn, son of Finnlug, of the race of Ciar'; 'And as Noah raised up the ark over the wave-voice of the flood on high, so then will Brenainn raise up his monks and his households on high over the fire of Doom, so that neither smoke, nor mist, nor spark will reach them'; 'Of Ciarraige Luachra was he, of Altraige Caille'

Lismore Life: 'Brenainn remained five years with Ita'; the angel: 'God hath given thee what thou soughtest, even the Land of Promise'; 'three great vessels', 'three sails of hides'; 'five years on the ocean'; Easter 'to the end of seven years, on the back of the whale'; 'the Devil there revealed the gate of hell to Brenainn'; Ita: 'thou wilt never find it after those dead stained skins'; 'a great marvellous vessel is built by him' in Connaught; 'they reached the land which they had been seeking for the space of seven years, even the Land of Promise'

Book of Lismore story (Stokes's description of the manuscript): 'Story of S. Brenainn ... harper and the bird-like angel'; 'Once when Brenainn maccu Altai was in Clonfert, on Easter-day seven years before his obit'; 'it is now seven years since Brenainn smiled or heard a melody of the melodies of the world'

Rees, Vita S. Brendani: 'filius Finloc, nepos Alti ... Hic erat vir magne abstinentie, et in virtutibus clarus, triumque millium fere monachorum pater fuit'; Barurchus tells of the Land of Promise of the Saints; Brendan chooses fourteen; Rees: 'The Manuscript here ends abruptly'; 'From the Cott. MSS ... Vespasian, A. XIV'

Rees: 'The time when these Lives were compiled, is not known, but it was probably about the twelfth century'; the appendix Lives 'were not of Cambro-British Saints, but were, notwithstanding, connected with Wales ... those of St. Aidus, St. Brendanus, and St. Tathan, the Saints, although natives of Ireland, had passed much of their time in the Welsh country'
Rees, Life of David: 'apparuit ubi Sanctus Brendanus super marinum cetum miram ducebat vitam'; Barre rides David's horse over the sea

O'Donovan, notes to the Four Masters: 'Clonfert, a bishop's see in the south-east of the county of Galway'; 'Clonfert-Brendan ... The church of Clonfert ... county of Galway'; O'Flaherty: 'Enaghdun, dedicated to St. Brendan, the 16th of May, Anno Christi 577, there deceased'; Birr 'founded ... by St. Brendan, the son of Neman, who died on the 29th of November, A. D. 572'; annal entry 'Bishop of Clonfert-Brendan' under 1173
claims.witness: four-masters odonovan1856 l.969-970, 4501-4503, 4245-4251, 15938-15941, 927 (year head 'THE AGE OF CHRIST, 1173' l.760); the file header marks the volume a second witness, to be checked against the scan

claims.claim: The bishops chose 'Mar Grégoire' (OCR 'Mar Gré égoire'; 'Mar Grégoire, catholicos, patriarche'); Chabot's note: 'Grégoire, originaire de Pherat'; Guidi's chronicle: 'catholicus factus est Gregorius, Phoráth oriundus'
claims.witness: Chabot (chabot1902 l.31473, 31485, 31528); anonymous chronicle, Latin by Guidi (chronica-minora guidi1903 l.1954)

claims.claim: Signature no. 27: 'Bar HaDbsES4884, évêque de Holwän' (OCR; Chabot's index reads 'Bar Hadbesabba (605)'); Braun: 'Barhadbsabbä B. v. H(o)lwän'. No epithet 'Arbaia in the signature. Page 479 of Chabot's French (page header OCR '47!)')

Scher identifies the signer with the author: 'il devint ensuite évêque de Halwan; et c'est en cette qualité qu'en 605 il assista au Synode de Grégoire patriarche'; Nau: 'un certain Bar Hadbesabba Arbaia, qui etait eveque de Halwan en 605, puisqu'il souscrivait a cette epoque le synode de Gregoire Ier, cf. Synodicon Orientale, Paris, 1902, p. 479' and 'Le meme eveque de Halwan a ecrit la Cause de la fondation des ecoles' (OCR 'svnode', 'Sijnodiro)!', and the last sentence badly garbled)
claims.witness: Scher, introduction (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.16973-16975); Nau, introduction (po09 l.31579-31581, 31598-31599)

claims.claim: The Cause's title as printed: 'MAR BARHADBSABBA ‘ARBAYA / ÉVÊQUE DE HALW'AN (VIE SIÈCLE)' and 'COMPOSÉE PAR MAR BARHADBSABBA ‘ARBAYA, ÉVÊQUE DE HALWAN'

Scher: 'L'auteur du traité, Barhadbšabba ‘Arbaya, était originaire de la région de Beith ‘Arbayé, ainsi que l'indique son surnom; il fit ses études dans l’école de Nisibe sous Hnana d’Adiabène (572-610 ?), ainsi qu'il le déclare lui-même dans son traité'

Assemani: 'Ba-Arbaja, oppidum in dioecesi Nisibena, unde Jesujabus Arzunita & Barhedbesciaba scriptores Sobensi in Catalogo laudati ortum duxere'; and on Abdisho's chapter: 'Beth-Arbaje, seu Ba-Arbaja pago apud Nisibin' (OCR 'Betb‘%Arba)e', 'Ni- fibio'); the card cites only BO III.1's 'near Nisibis' (R1 D-B3)
claims.witness: Assemani, BO III.2 (assemani tomus3-pars2 1728 l.49913-49916, OCR long s); BO III.1 (assemani tomus3-pars1 1725 l.30868-30870)

claims.claim: Nau on the name: 'Ce nom signifie « le fils du dimanche ». Il est analogue a Cyriaque et a Dominique'; Assemani: 'filius diei Dominicae'
claims.witness: Nau's note 2 (po09 l.31593); Assemani (tomus3-pars1 l.30854-30860, OCR 'Doroinies')

claims.claim: Scher's summary: the treaty covers 'les différentes écoles, comme le dit l’auteur, par lesquelles Dieu a bien voulu instruire les anges et les hommes', the schools for the angels, Adam, Cain and Abel, Noah, Abraham, the Israelites, Solomon, the prophets, the philosophers, Jesus Christ, the apostles, Alexandria and Antioch; 'il fait enfin l’histoire des deux écoles syriaques d’Édesse et de Nisibe. Le récit de l’auteur sur ces deux écoles, surtout sur la dernière, est très précieux. C'est le premier ouvrage qui nous retrace l’histoire de la plus célèbre de toutes les écoles de la Chaldée'; the earlier part 'est d'une prolixité fastidieuse'

The Cause on Henana: 'Il fut remplacé par Hnana d'Adiabène, homme orné d'humilité'; 'ayant vidé tout son carquois sur le parti du démon, celui-ci fit éclater contre lui de terribles agitations'; 'il s'appliquait jour et nuit à la lecture et à l'interprétation des Écritures'; 'Nous prions tous Dieu de prolonger ses jours'

Scher: 'Il est probable que l’auteur dissimule ici la vérité pour louer son maitre auprès de ses coreligionnaires. Car les Nestoriens ont toujours accusé Hnana d'avoir abandonné dans ses commentaires les sentences de Théodore de Mopsueste'

Chronicle of Seert: the students left the school ('Les etudiants furent fortement affectes de cette decision de Sabriso', qui avait repousse la parole du metropolitain pour accepter celle de Hnana ... ils sortirent de l'Ecole'), 'environ trois cents' (OCR 'eiiviron'); 'Parmi ceux qui sortirent de l'Ecole de Nisibe, il y avait Isoyahb de Gdala ... Hadbsabba 'Arbaya, [qui] fut fait metropolitain de Houlwan'; Scher's notes: 'Ou plutot Barhadbsabba' and 'C'est en cette qualite qu'en 605 il assista au synode de Gregoire'; the identification with the Cause's author is Scher's, and the brief says so
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert, tr. Scher (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.28671-28674, 28707, 28720-28721, 28731, 28756, 28774; OCR 'fureiit', 'TEcoIe', '»1111 fut fiiit metropolitain do lloulwan')

claims.claim: Scher: 'Mais pourquoi Barhadbšabba se serait-il séparé de son maître Hnana, lui qui, quelques années auparavant, s'était montré son admirateur et avait même appelé ses adversaires « ouailles de satan » ? On peut conjecturer qu'il suivit le parti le plus fort'; and he may have written 'surtout pour ramener la paix et la concorde dans la Congrégation'

Nau: the History's author 'etait « pretre et chef des surveillants (...) de la sainte ecole de la ville de Nisibe » d'apres le titre de l'ouvrage, et « originaire du Beit-Arbaie, pretre et interprete » d'apres la finale. Il semble donc identique a Barhadbesabba 'Arbaia ... mentionne par Ebedjesu'; its exact title is 'Histoire des saints Peres persecutes a cause de la verite'; it 'a donc toute chance d'avoir ete ecrite a la fin du vie siecle'. Nau's note 1 reports the word for 'overseers' rendered elsewhere as 'professeur' and 'professeur de philosophie'.

Nau: 'Il n'est pas impossible que notre auteur de « l'Histoire des saints Peres », identique a l'auteur cite par Ebedjesu, soit encore identique a l'eveque de Halwan. Il suffit de supposer qu'il a ecrit « l'Histoire des saints Peres » dans sa jeunesse ... et qu'il a prononce ou ecrit le discours sur la Cause de la fondation des ecoles dans sa vieillesse'

Abdisho's catalogue, ch. XCIII 'Barhadbesciaba Arabs': 'Scripsit librum Thesaurorum In tres tomos distributum: Et disputationes Adversus omnes sectas, earumque confutationem; Ecclesiasticam praeterea historiam; necnon de causa Sectatorum Mar Diodori; Commentarium denique in Marcum Evangelistam, & Davidem'; Nau gives the same list in French
claims.witness: Assemani, BO III.1 (tomus3-pars1 1725 l.30771-30794, OCR long s and 'ptretereif/^or/flw'); Nau (po09 l.31565-31567)

claims.claim: Scher gives this list to the Cause's author and notes 'qu Ebedjésus ne mentionne pas ici le traité de Barhadbšabba sur les écoles ... Ebedjésus n'aurait donc pas eu connaissance du traité'

Dating the Cause. Scher: 'postérieure à l’avènement de Išo‘yahb d'Arzoun, qui eut lieu en 581 ... aussi antérieure à 604'; the editors' note: 'un « discours d'ouverture de la session des écoles » à Nisibe vers l’an de grâce 590'; Connolly: 'It is probable then that the chronicle was written some little time after the year 585'
claims.witness: Scher (scher1908 l.17018-17023); 'Note des éditeurs' (l.17102, 17118-17131); Connolly (narsai connolly1909 l.308-314)

claims.claim: The editors' note is headed '[Note des éditeurs' (OCR 'Nore pes éprreurs'); the series editors are R. Graffin and F. Nau (file header); the card names the note's writers as 'the editors of the Patrologia Orientalis' and does not name them singly

Mingana and Chabot on the Cause: 'M. Mingana croit que ce document est une partie de l’histoire de Barhadbšabba. M. Chabot le croit être une juxtaposition mal coordonnée de deux ou plusieurs récits antérieurs'; Scher: 'Le traité ne fait nullement partie de l'histoire de Barhadbšabba'; 'Rien ne nous empêche d'accorder à cet ouvrage une entière confiance'; the troubling passages inserted 'par un copiste quelconque'

Guidi's chronicle, after Gregory of Phorath's death and the long vacancy: 'Ea aetate claruerunt in ecclesia Ionadab adiabenus ... Nominis famam adeptus erat in libris conscribendis Bàr Hadhbésabba urbis Holwan; moribus autem vitae eximiis clarebat Subhhalémáran urbis Karkha dhé Beth Sélokh, et Afrahnoy(?) regionis ad fluvios Zabh, et Gabriel urbis Néhargul'. Nau's French of the line: 'Bar Hadbesabba de Halwan etait celebre dans la litterature et brillait dans les oeuvres de la perfection'. Braun's German of Guidi agrees with the Latin split ('Durch vorzüglichen Lebenswandel zeichneten sich aus:.... G. v. N.')
claims.witness: chronica-minora guidi1903 l.1954-1979 (OCR 'lonadab'); Nau (po09 l.31582-31587); Braun (braun1900 l.14934-14935)

claims.claim: The vacancy: Nau 'entre les annees 609 et 628'; Scher 'pendant la vacance forcée du siège patriarcal (609-628)'; Chabot: Gregory died 'entre oct. 608 avril 609'

Scher: 'Il mourut probablement dans la première moitié du vi[i]e siècle' (OCR 'vi siè-cle'; the sense must be the seventh century, since the next clause has him alive during the vacancy of 609-628); not used on the card after R1 (D-M6), since the scan reads 'vi'
Labourt: 'Barhadbešabba de Holwan, écrivain distingué', with note 1: 'Cet évêque est peut-être celui que Sabrišo‘ avait désigné pour lui succéder'

Connolly's English of the Cause: 'Edessa was darkened, but Nisibis shone forth ; and the dominions of the Romans were filled with error, but those of Persia with the knowledge of true religion' (the brief closes the space before the semicolon); Scher's French: 'Édesse s’obscurcit; Nisibe s’illumina: l'empire des Romains s’emplit d'erreur, celui des Perses de la connaissance de la crainte de Dieu'
claims.witness: Connolly (narsai connolly1909 l.4494-4496, citing 'Barhadhbeshabba Chron. apud Mingana, Preface p. 35', l.4523); Cause, tr. Scher (scher1908 l.20743-20746)

claims.claim: Connolly: 'a fragment of a chronicle by Barhadhbeshabba (saec. VI—VII) which is of first-rate importance for the history of the Nestorian School of Nisibis'; 'If with Mingana we adopt this reckoning ... his death will fall in 502'

Scher trusts the Cause over later witnesses: on Elisha, 'Barhadbšabba, qui est beaucoup plus digne de foi, ayant écrit ce traité à la fin du VIe siècle, dit ici clairement qu'il n'a pas été évêque'; on Narsai's forty-five years, 'plus digne de foi que R. Sourin'

Nau on the History: 'la presente histoire parait etre la plus ancienne histoire ecclesiastique nestorienne et elle a ete utilisee par tous les auteurs posterieurs ... elle est encore la source de la legende syriaque de Nestorius'; its chapters XIX-XXXII run from Theodore of Mopsuestia and Nestorius through Ephesus to 'Mar Narses, pretre et docteur' and 'Mar Abraham, pretre et docteur'; Nau: 'Cette histoire des saints Peres, qui se termine avec Abraham (+ 569)'

Namesake, the monk of Mount Sa'ran: Seert 'Celui-ci [Sabrisho] avait recommande aux fideles de choisir Barhadbsabba le moine qui habitait la montagne de Sa'ran'; Mari 'etsi Mar Sabarjesus mandavisset in patriarcham assumi Barhadbsabba monachum in monte Sa'aran habitantem' (OCR 'habilanlem'); Hoffmann 'Barhadhbsabbä, einem Mönche auf dem Gebirge Sa'rän'; Braun after Mari 'den Rabban Barhadbšabbā vom Gebel Saran'
claims.witness: Seert (scher1919 l.29180-29181); Mari, Latin by Gismondi (mari-ibn-sulayman gismondi1899 l.13591-13592, OCR 'nmnte'); Hoffmann (hoffmann1880 l.6298-6299); Braun (braun1900 l.14496-14497)

claims.claim: Assemani: 'Diversus proinde ab eo Barhadbesciaba videtur, qui Jacobo Beth-Abensis coenobii fundatori aequalis fuit, teste Margensi'
claims.witness: Assemani, BO III.1 (tomus3-pars1 1725 l.30871-30875, OCR 'Diverfua croinde', '£qualis', 'tefie')

claims.claim: Other namesakes: 'Barhadbešabba, diacre d’Arbel' (a martyr under Shapur); 'un certain Barhadbešabba de Qardu'; 'Bar Hadbsaba, archimandritae et fratribus' in Ishoyahb III's letters
claims.witness: Labourt (labourt1904 l.4839, 7834); Ishoyahb III, Latin by Duval (ishoyahb-iii duval1905 l.5517, 11494)

claims.claim: Card framing after R1 (coordinator's ruling): the History is filed as the work of Barhadbeshabba 'Arbaia of the school of Nisibis, not as this bishop's; it appears on the card only in `uncertain` and in Nau's introduction under `about`. Display name 'Barhadbeshabba 'Arbaia of Halwan' keeps him apart from the History's writer of batch 1.
claims.witness: Nau (po09 l.31557-31561, 31601-31607); batch 1 narsai and barsauma-of-nisibis cards

contested_claims.claim: Whether the author of the History and the author of the Cause are one man
sides: Nau: the History is by Barhadbeshabba 'Arbaia, priest and head of the overseers of the school of Nisibis, and it is 'pas impossible' that he is the bishop of Halwan who wrote the Cause, young for the History and old for the Cause (po09 l.31557-31561, 31601-31607)

Scher treats them as one, giving the Cause's author Abdisho's list of books with its history, and speaking of 'l'histoire de Barhadbšabba' as the same author's (scher1908 l.16980-16984, 17054, 17088-17093); the PO 9 and PO 4 file headers also name the History's author 'bishop of Halwan', a Library metadata choice

contested_claims.claim: When the Cause was written
sides: Scher: after Ishoyahb of Arzun's accession (581 by Scher) and before 604 (scher1908 l.17018-17023)
Connolly: a little after 585 (connolly1909 l.308-314)
The PO editors' note: about 590, as an opening address (scher1908 l.17118-17131)

contested_claims.claim: Bishop or metropolitan of Halwan
sides: Bishop: the synod's signature (chabot1902 l.31930; braun1900 l.14917) and the Cause's title (scher1908 l.17169-17170)
Metropolitan: the Chronicle of Seert, 'fut fait metropolitain de Houlwan' (scher1919 l.28756)

contested_claims.claim: What Guidi's chronicle says of him
sides: Guidi's Latin and Braun's German: fame for writing books, with excellence of life given to Subhalmaran and others (guidi1903 l.1975-1978; braun1900 l.14934-14935)
Nau's French: celebrated in literature and shining in works of perfection (po09 l.31586-31587)

contested_claims.claim: Whether the bishop of Holwan is the monk of Mount Sa'ran whom Sabrisho wanted as successor
sides: Labourt: 'peut-être' (labourt1904 l.12702-12703)

Seert, Mari, Hoffmann and Braun name the monk with no link to Holwan, and the Cause's author was a student at Nisibis by Scher's account (scher1919 l.29180-29181; gismondi1899 l.13592; scher1908 l.16930-16934)

absent_details.detail: His birth, family, ordination and death
absent_details.note: Searched all of cic/texts for Hadb, Hadhb, Hadbe, dbsab, dbefc/dbelc/dbcfc (Assemani's long-s forms), Halwan, Holwan, Hulwan, Houlwan, Arbai, Arbay, Beth Arbaye. No held line gives his birth, family, the year of his consecration or of his death. Scher's 'first half of the seventh century' is an inference from the 605 signature and Guidi's chronicle.

absent_details.detail: His other books
absent_details.note: The Treasures, the controversies against all sects, the work on the followers of Diodore and the commentary on Mark and the Psalms, listed by Abdisho, are not held. Of the History only the second part (chapters XIX-XXXII, Nau, PO 9) is held; Nau's promised first part (chapters I-XVIII) is not. Mingana's Syriac edition of the Cause is not held; Connolly's English gives a few passages of it only.

absent_details.note: Known only from Nau's introduction (po09 l.31558-31559); the OCR of the History's end in the held file does not recover it (searched 'Beit', 'Arba', 'interprete' in the History's range).

absent_details.note: None held. The census lists a modern English translation of the Cause (Liverpool UP) as a source note, not as a held file. Connolly's English covers a few passages.

claims.claim: §4: 'Quand ils apportèrent cette lettre à Alexandrie et que le (subactor ? ) la faisait lire au lecteur, je vins par derrière et la regardai, j'y lus les noms de ces mauvais conseillers. Je retournai alors près de notre père Dioscore, puis je lui dis avec les paroles des fils des prophètes : « La mort est dans cette lettre, ô homme de Dieu »'; the counsellors are Ibas of Edessa, 'Théodore de Cyr' and Andrew of Samosata, whom Marcian 'louait et les exaltait comme ses conseillers'; Nau's note: 'Cf. IV, Rois, iv, 40'. The brief tells it in reported speech. The brief says he 'came up from behind and looked at it' (je vins par derrière et la regardai) and names the counselors as the men the emperor praised as his counselors (l.13928-13930).
claims.witness: theopistus (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903) l.13925-13930, 13950-13956 (OCR 'celte' for cette, 'fds' for fils, '6' for ô); note l.13980

claims.claim: Title of the translation: 'Histoire du saint divin mar Dioscore, patriarche de tous les orthodoxes et archevêque d'Alexandrie, écrite par son disciple Théopiste'; §1 opens 'Mes amis, j'apprends à votre affection quels rudes combats nous avons soutenus, moi et mon père saint Dioscore l'archevêque'. Told as the book's account: the narrator names himself.

The narrator names himself: §11 'Alors moi Théopiste, je portai cette lettre au concile'; §20 Dioscorus says 'Théopiste, mon fils, après ma mort laisse Pierre près de mon corps et sauve-toi, car un grand danger te menacera'.

Deacon: §14 the brother he sends to beg says 'Le diacre de Dioscore, l'archevêque d'Alexandrie, te demande une petite aumône'; the merchant answers him 'Seigneur diacre n'aie pas honte'; §16 the healed man cries 'Vive le Dieu de ce diacre d'Alexandrie !'. Nau: 'l'histoire de Dioscore nous apprend qu'il avait avec lui l'archidiacre Pierre et le diacre Théopiste'. The card name 'Theopistus, deacon of Dioscorus' rests on these lines.
claims.witness: theopistus (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903) l.16048-16049, 16073-16074, 16395; Nau's note l.878-880 (OCR 'Tbéopiste' l.878)

claims.claim: Nau: 'A partir de la convocation du concile, Théopiste prétend n'avoir plus quitté Dioscore. A la mort de celui-ci, et pour éviter une arrestation, il se réfugie dans la ville de Pentapolis (la Pentapole?) et y écrit aussitôt la présente histoire (§20). D'ailleurs, il se met parfois en scène (§4 et 11), raconte, de manière assez simple, comment il reçut un soufflet de celui qui devait les conduire en exil (§10); comment il en fut réduit à mendier pour vivre (§14) et comment il opéra un miracle avec le sang de Dioscore (§16).' The brief names the council as Chalcedon (Nau l.178-179) and the bishop's death in exile from the History: 'c'est pour elle que je meurs en exil' (l.17012-17013).
claims.witness: Nau's introduction, theopistus (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903) l.441-471 (OCR '$ 20', 'S 4', 'S 10', '5 1 6'); l.178-179; l.17012-17013

claims.claim: §10, the slap: the envoy mocks Dioscorus; 'Quand je vis qu'ils interpellaient ce saint vieillard, je pleurai et dis à cet envoyé maudit : « Je te prie de ne pas te moquer de lui, car il est peu robuste... » — Quand l'un des hérétiques m'entendit parler, il courut sur moi, me donna un soufflet'. The History has 'one of the heretics' slap him; Nau's summary (l.448-449) gives it to the man who was to take them into exile. The brief follows the History.

§20: 'Et deux mois après sa mort saint Pierre m'envoya une lettre : « Va, fuis et cache-toi ». — Car lorsque les hérétiques apprirent la mort de notre saint père Dioscore le patriarche, ils dirent de moi à l'empereur que l'or et l'argent des églises étaient cachés chez moi... Aussitôt j'allai à la ville de Pentépolis, m'y cachai et y écrivis cette histoire'; Nau's note: 'Ou plutôt : Dans la Pentapole (Cyrénaïque).' The brief calls this Peter 'the archdeacon Peter': §20 names 'l'archidiacre Pierre' a few lines before (l.16922-16923), and he is the only Peter with them in the narrative; the line itself says 'saint Pierre'. The brief keeps 'two months after' and tells the hiding and writing as the narrator's own statement ('He says he hid'), since Nau's reworking view disputes it.
claims.witness: theopistus (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903) l.17022-17031 (OCR 'Pen- tépolis'); note l.17034 (OCR 'On plutôt')

claims.claim: Death date in the History: 'Il dit et rendit son âme à Dieu à onze heures de la nuit du quatre du mois d'Elul « septembre »'; no year. Nau: Dioscorus 'mourut le 4 septembre 454'. Duchesne: 'Dioscore mourait à Gangres, le 4 septembre 454, après trois années d'exil'.
Gangra an island: 'on nous conduisit dans l'île appelée Gangara (Gangra)'; 'l'île de Gangara'.

Close: 'Je témoigne devant Dieu que j'ai écrit la vérité, et maintenant croyez, mes frères, que je n'ai pas écrit tous les prodiges, toutes les guérisons et tous les miracles que Dieu opéra par les mains de ce saint martyr de la vérité parce qu'il y en a trop.' A prayer follows, then 'Fin de l'histoire'; hence 'near the end'.

Nau: 'Cependant, Dioscore, dans une vision, apprend que Sévère sera patriarche d'Antioche (§19), ce qui place la composition de la présente rédaction après l'an 512'; note 'Sévère fut patriarche de 512 à 518'. The vision itself (§19): Cyril asks Ignatius to bless 'mon fils', and Ignatius places his hand 'sur la tête d'un petit enfant' and says 'Sévère, viens voir tes pères et imite leurs actions'. The brief tells the vision and gives the patriarchate as Nau's reading. The vision is Dioscorus's own ('J'ai vu cette nuit', l.16865-16866); the brief gives 512 as the year Severus took the see, from Nau's note (l.498).
claims.witness: Nau theopistus (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903) l.484-487, 498 (OCR '5 ia', '5i2 à 5 i 8'); the vision l.16871-16916

claims.claim: Nau's solution: 'Peu après la mort de Dioscore, on écrivit en Égypte un certain nombre de récits en sa faveur, parmi ceux-ci pouvait se trouver un récit, écrit par Théopiste, de la réunion du concile de Chalcédoine et de l'exil à Gangres. Après l'an 512, l'un des rhéteurs de l'école de Pierre l'Ibère reprit l'écrit de Théopiste et le compléta à l'aide de ses connaissances personnelles. Ce remaniement fut sans doute rédigé en grec ... et d'ailleurs le syriaque que nous publions semble être une traduction du grec. Enfin ce remaniement grec fut traduit en syriaque avec quelques nouvelles modifications et constitua enfin la présente histoire.' He calls it 'la solution suivante comme la plus probable pour l'instant'. The brief tells it as a suggestion: Theopistus 'may have written' an account, which may have been among the 'récits en sa faveur' (l.582); 'rhéteurs' is told as 'a writer trained in rhetoric'. Peter the Iberian is placed on the card as bishop of Maiouma near Gaza (Nau's note l.15346-15347).

Nau's grounds for Greek: Greek words transcribed, the forms of some names (Paphnutios for Coptic Paphnuti), and the Palestinian passages, which 'n'ont aucune chance d'avoir été rédigés en copte'; scripture 'semblent traduits directement sur un texte grec', but one passage (§15; I Peter v, 3) is 'cité d'après la Peschito' and 'n'a donc pu être introduit que par un Syrien'.
claims.witness: Nau theopistus (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903) l.544-554, 577; note l.597-620 (Greek and Syriac OCR garbled)

claims.claim: Peter 'now a priest': §6 'Quand mon père eut lu cette lettre, il me dit ainsi qu'à l'archidiacre Pierre, lequel est maintenant prêtre'; Nau: 'si donc on admet, comme l'a écrit M. claims.claim: Crum note: 'M. Crum a trouvé des fragments coptes anciens qui correspondent aux paragraphes 7, 13, 18, 19 (?) et 20 de la présente histoire; ils serviront à rechercher avec plus de sûreté quel est le texte original et à préciser l'ordre de filiation des versions.' The note is unsigned, in Nau's article; the card does not give it to Nau by name, and says only that 'it says' the fragments will help in working out which text is the original ('serviront à rechercher avec plus de sûreté').

The History of the Patriarchs: 'In this way no biography of the holy patriarch Dioscorus after his banishment has been found'; it says Mennas wrote 'of what the Father Dioscorus after him suffered in the council of Chalcedon'. It does not name Theopistus.

The synaxaries' entries on Dioscorus tell of the exile with Macarius and do not name Theopistus: Arabic Jacobite (Basset), 7 Tout: 'il partit et avec lui Macaire évêque d'Edkou'; Ethiopic (Budge): 'with him was Abba MACARIUS, bishop of the city of KAw'.

Namesake, kept apart: 'Remember me, even me, Theopistos, the feeble one, the deacon, the son of Severus the archpresbyter of Saint Mercurius of the city of Sne. I wrote this book with my own hand', in the colophon of Brit. Mus. MS. Oriental 7024, which Budge dates 'a. d. 985'.
Namesake, kept apart: 'Theopistus, filius divi Eustathii, martir' (index); the Roman Breviary's 'Eustace, Agapitus, Theopistus, and Theopista, Martyrs'.

Later notes by Nau name him only as the History's writer: 'l'Histoire de Dioscore, écrite par son disciple Théopiste (Paris, 1903)' (1912); 'F. Nau, Histoire de Dioscore, écrite par son disciple Théopiste' (PO 13 note).
Gangra in Paphlagonia: the Coptic panegyric, as Nau quotes it, 'exilé à Gangres, île de la Paphlagonie'.

contested_claims.claim: Who wrote the History of Dioscorus as it survives
contested_claims.sides: The book itself: its narrator names himself Theopistus, the disciple of Dioscorus, and says he wrote it in hiding at Pentapolis two months after the death (title l.13482-13485; §11 l.15582; §20 l.17022-17031). Nau, in his view 'la plus probable pour l'instant': an account by Theopistus 'pouvait se trouver' among accounts written in Egypt soon after the death; after 512 a rhetor of Peter the Iberian's school reworked and completed it, probably in Greek; the Greek was then put into Syriac with further changes (l.577-595, 636-637); in 1912 he adds that the reviser used the Plerophories (po08 l.442). Nau also notes the line making the archdeacon Peter 'maintenant prêtre', which would put the account before 477 if Peter is Peter Mongus, as Revillout wrote (l.471-477). Assemani, as Nau quotes him: 'Fabulosa narratio a jacobitis recentioribus excogitata' (l.503-504); Nau rejects the later-forgery view (l.530-542).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Coptic panegyric of Macarius of Tkow was written by Peter and Theopistus
contested_claims.sides: Its own title, in Nau's French: 'Pierre et Théopiste, les diacres qui l'avaient suivi ont écrit cet (éloge)' (l.807-808). Nau: the panegyric depends on the History and took the two names from it (l.739-742, 877-883). Duchesne reports that Amélineau showed it to be apocryphal and of no value (duchesne tome3 l.15897-15907).
